correctness.rationale: The inverse-positive M-matrix property is exact from the finite Neumann series. The field-of-values boundary is the exact smallest Hermitian-part eigenvalue. The first and second GMRES iterates are reconstructed from the defining normal equations, with a positive Gram determinant. Analytic sign bounds prove that the fourth coordinate alone crosses at t=1 inside 0<t<sqrt(5)-1. Exact rational replay at t=6/5 returns VERIFY_OK.

originality.rationale: Classical GMRES residual minimization, Krylov-polynomial representations, nonnormality, and field-of-values convergence are treated as prior work. The accepted statement is the exact separation, on an inverse-positive four-state M-matrix family, between the second-iterate orthant boundary t=1 and the right-half-plane numerical-range boundary t=sqrt(5)-1. Searches across coordinate-positivity, M-matrix, Jordan-family, residual-polynomial, and numerical-range aliases did not locate an implication-equivalent result.
residual_risks: Older positivity-preserving Krylov, monotone matrix-iteration, or M-matrix literature may contain a related sign-loss example under different terminology.
Only the opening material of the 1992 technical report and abstract-level material of the original GMRES paper were inspected; no claim of exhaustive historical coverage is made.
No minimal-dimension claim is made, and no claim is made about later iterates or general M-matrices.

value.rationale: M-matrices model many discretized positive systems, where nonnegative exact solutions carry physical meaning. The result shows that inverse positivity, a positive exact solution, a spectrum fixed entirely at 1, first-step positivity, and right-half-plane numerical-range separation still do not protect GMRES coordinates. The exact gap from t=1 to t=sqrt(5)-1 provides a sharp, reproducible boundary rather than a generic warning.
